Counting according to the three scoring regions of the target: Tom has 3 arrows in the inner layer, 1 in the middle layer, and 2 in the outer layer; John has 1 arrow in the inner layer, 3 in the middle layer, and 2 in the outer layer; Lily has 2 arrows in the inner layer, 2 in the middle layer, and 2 in the outer layer. Therefore Lily's score is the average of Tom and John's scores, namely (46 + 34) / 2 = 40.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the three targets show the counts of arrows in the three scoring sections. Tom has 3 arrows in the inner section, 1 in the middle section, and 2 in the outer section. John has 1 inner, 3 middle, and 2 outer. Lily has 2 inner, 2 middle, and 2 outer. From the text, Tom's total is 46 and John's total is 34, and points depend only on which section is hit. Notice that Lily's count in each section is exactly the average of Tom's and John's counts: inner (3+1)/2=2, middle (1+3)/2=2, outer (2+2)/2=2. Therefore Lily's score is the average of their scores: (46+34)/2=40.
